Commit 0e55c4f9be changed the Prepare header's "Printer settings…" to open the printer conversation panel instead of OrcaSlicer's settings window, but tests/shell/shell_harness.cpp verify_header_setup / verify_header_setup_open still expects the settings window. name: jusprin-worktree-build
description: How to configure a JusPrin worktree build reusing existing deps; BUILD_TESTS=ON needed for tests
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: 01c34c35-1546-40fb-a600-c49b2e1ffa06
  modified: 2026-09-14T14:18:48.216Z
---

A JusPrin git worktree builds against the already-built deps by configuring:

```
cmake -B build/arm64 -G "Ninja Multi-Config" -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DCMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES=arm64 -DCMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=15.0 \
  -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH="/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local;/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local" \
  -DSLIC3R_GUI=ON -DSLIC3R_STATIC=ON -DSLIC3R_PCH=ON -DBUILD_TESTS=ON \
  -DCMAKE_AR=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar -DCMAKE_RANLIB=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ranlib
```

The two `CMAKE_AR`/`CMAKE_RANLIB` flags are required on a FRESH build dir:
without them Apple's ar is used and liblibslic3r_gui.a (>4 GiB in
RelWithDebInfo) fails to archive. They only work at first configure, not on
reconfigure. Full story: agent-docs/macos-build-troubleshooting.md. See
[[liblibslic3r-gui-4gib-ar-limit]].

`BUILD_TESTS=ON` is required or the tests/ tree (workspace, shell targets) is
not generated. Build with `cmake --build build/arm64 --config RelWithDebInfo
--target <targets>`. wxWidgets 3.3 sources for API verification live under
/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/dep_wxWidgets-prefix/.

CWD TRAP (cost real time once): the harness resets the Bash cwd to the main
repo /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin between turns, so a *relative*
`cmake --build build/arm64` silently builds the MAIN repo's build dir, not the
worktree's — the worktree binary then runs stale code and a re-fix looks like it
"didn't take". Always pass the worktree build dir as an ABSOLUTE path to
`cmake --build /…/.claude/worktrees/<wt>/build/arm64 …`, and run test binaries by
absolute path. Also: `cmake --build --target <one_exe>` may relink against a
stale lib without recompiling a changed .cpp in that lib — build the app target
(e.g. OrcaSlicer) too so the lib recompiles; verify with
`grep -c '<file>.cpp.o' build.log`. Editing tools (Edit/Write) use absolute
paths so source edits land correctly regardless of cwd.

name: liblibslic3r-gui-4gib-ar-limit
description: "RelWithDebInfo liblibslic3r_gui.a crossed Apple ar's 4 GiB archive limit on jusprin-newui (2026-09-13); CMAKE_AR override is ignored; manual llvm-ar relink recipe and its cd trap"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 0771473f-5d46-4419-b8e5-112938ea6b34
  modified: 2026-09-14T14:18:50.456Z
---

On 2026-09-13, at jusprin-newui 770bd2b0a2 (after "Add the evidence-led Add a
printer flow"), a worktree RelWithDebInfo build failed archiving
`src/slic3r/RelWithDebInfo/liblibslic3r_gui.a`:
`Assertion failed: (memberOffset < 0xFFFFFFFF) ... ArchiveWriter.cpp` then
`fatal error in .../ranlib`. The archive llvm-ar produced was 4,309,350,176
bytes; the main checkout's copy built minutes earlier was 4,143,827,796 and
still fit. Objects are big because the root CMakeLists.txt (lines ~544-548)
rewrites RelWithDebInfo -O2 to -O0 on purpose. Disk space was not the cause.

**Why:** the failed build left the OLD harness binary in place, and the harness
runs afterwards "passed" against stale code (a new `--printer-setup` flag
silently ran the default mode: same 285 check count). Gate runs on build
success and compare binary mtime.

**How to apply:**
- `-DCMAKE_AR=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar` on an existing build dir does
  nothing: `CMakeFiles/<ver>/CMakeCXXCompiler.cmake` sets CMAKE_AR as a normal
  variable that shadows the cache.
- Working relink: `ninja -f build-RelWithDebInfo.ninja -t commands <target>`,
  drop compile lines, swap ar/ranlib for llvm-ar/llvm-ranlib on the gui archive
  line only, then run EACH line in its own `(cd build/arm64 && eval "$line")`.
  One `sh` script fails with bogus "no such file" errors because the
  encoding-check line does `cd src/slic3r` and it leaks; `sh -e` also does not
  stop inside `&&` chains. Apple's linker accepted the >4 GiB llvm-ar archive.
- The fix is PER BUILD DIRECTORY, nothing in the repo selects llvm-ar. Main
  checkout's build/arm64 cache has llvm-ar (commit 449b676145 documents it in
  agent-docs/macos-build-troubleshooting.md); any newly configured build dir
  gets Apple ar and fails again. Configure new dirs with the flags in
  [[jusprin-worktree-build]].
- Recurred 2026-09-14 on a fresh worktree at jusprin-newui bc19661a7f (archive
  4,308,513,464 bytes). Shortcut that worked: after the failed build, from
  `-t commands shell_integration_harness` drop lines containing ` -c `; only
  the last two remain relevant (gui archive, then harness link). Run just
  those two, swapping ar/ranlib on the archive line. Harness then passed.
- A lasting fix (llvm-ar in the toolchain, thin archives, or less debug info)
  is Kenneth's call; the main checkout will hit this on its next growth.

Related: [[jusprin-worktree-build]], [[track-wall-clock-on-background-work]].

name: workspace-harness-never-post-inits-on-mac
description: "On macOS the workspace adapter harness never reaches GUI_App::post_init; closing its frame crashes, so it exits via ExitMainLoop unless post_initialized()"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: ed4bbcf2-a467-44f4-bceb-b20f93cd25d8
  modified: 2026-09-17T16:28:53.409Z
---

Found 2026-09-17 while fixing the journey-tools branch (merged to jusprin-newui as 35eb1b4a59).

`tests/workspace/real_adapter_harness.cpp` does its work in one synchronous run. On macOS, Orca adds each web view's script handler from a CallAfter (`src/slic3r/GUI/Widgets/WebView.cpp`) that runs a script and waits on the page in a nested event loop. In this harness the first one never returns, so `is_adding_script_handler()` stays true, the later views pile up in the static `g_delay_webviews`, and `post_init` (gated on that flag in `GUI_App.cpp`) never runs, even if the harness waits for it (it times out at 180 s).

Closing the main frame ends that wait; the deferred view setup (use-after-free on destroyed views) and then `post_init` (on a destroyed frame) run and segfault (exit 139) after `HARNESS RESULT PASS`. The harness therefore closes the frame only when `post_initialized()` (true on Windows, where the handler is added synchronously) and otherwise calls `ExitMainLoop()`.

**Why:** a Windows fix switched the exit to `Close(true)` and made every macOS run crash; an Orca-side fix (drop destroyed views from `g_delay_webviews`) removed only one of the two crashes.

**How to apply:** if the workspace harness crashes on exit, look here first; don't make it wait for post_init. The shell harness is unaffected because its checks are asynchronous. Related: [[orca-inherited-teardown-crash]], [[background-bash-timeout-kills-builds]].

name: subagent-worktrees-create-manually
description: "Agent tool isolation:\"worktree\" cut worktrees from a stale base and SendMessage was disabled; create worktrees by hand on the intended commit and pass absolute paths"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 598f26fe-b466-4336-928e-14d10d45e1f7
  modified: 2026-09-08T16:33:59.964Z
---

On 2026-09-08, three subagents launched with `isolation: "worktree"` got
worktrees at 095fb66576, an old commit with no JusPrin shell code, not the
branch tip they were told to expect. All three stopped correctly. SendMessage
was disabled in that session, so they could not be redirected; relaunching
was the only option.

**Why:** the isolation worktree is not cut from the current worktree's HEAD.
And `jusprin-newui` is rebased by other sessions while work is in flight, so
"base on newui" must be a specific commit, not a branch name.

**How to apply:** `git worktree add <path> -b <branch> <sha>` yourself, then
give the agent the absolute path and the expected SHA, and tell it to stop if
HEAD differs. Tell every agent the shell cwd may reset to the main checkout,
so all paths must be absolute. Before landing on `jusprin-newui`, read
`git reflog show jusprin-newui --date=relative`; if it moved in the last few
minutes another session is rebasing it. Land by cherry-pick, never
fast-forward, and expect your own commits to have new hashes afterwards.
See [[bash-cwd-resets-after-background]] and [[track-wall-clock-on-background-work]].

name: webview-destroyed-mid-handler-install
description: macOS crash when a wxWebView is destroyed while Orca's deferred AddScriptMessageHandler waits in a nested wxYield; guard with is_adding_script_handler()

Found 2026-09-18 (printer-setup shell harness exit 139 after PASS, at 0e55c4f9be).

Orca's `WebView::CreateWebView` (src/slic3r/GUI/Widgets/WebView.cpp) installs each view's "wx" message handler from a `CallAfter`. On macOS wx's `AddScriptMessageHandler` then runs a *synchronous* `RunScript`, which spins `wxYield` until WebKit answers, with `GUI_App::is_adding_script_handler()` true. Any pending CallAfter can run inside that yield. If it destroys that web view, WebKit later cancels the reply and calls `SendScriptResult` on the freed view → segfault in `wxEvtHandler::SafelyProcessEvent`. The JusPrin bridge's own sends are NOT the cause: `WebView::RunScript` on Mac uses `WKWebView_evaluateJavaScript` with no completion.

**Why:** a panel opened and closed within one event-loop turn (harness, or fast clicks) tears down before the install finishes.

**How to apply:** never delete a web view (or its owner) while `is_adding_script_handler()` is true. Hide it, cut its callbacks, and retry on a timer, as `PrinterPanel::tear_down_runtime` does (branch claude/printer-panel-exit-crash) and as `GUI_App::run_wizard` already did. Any other short-lived AgentWebView owner needs the same guard. Related: [[workspace-harness-never-post-inits-on-mac]], [[agent-setup-embedded-in-printer-dialog]].

I fixed both problems and verified each fix with the shell harness on commit 0e55c4f9be. Printer-setup mode now exits 0 in 3 of 3 runs (it was exit 139 in 3 of 3 before). Default mode now passes all 409 checks and exits 0 (before, it hung at the header check). The changes are not committed.

**Where the work is.** Another session was editing and running the harness in `printer-conversation-panel-af11cb` while I worked, including uncommitted edits to the same files I needed. So I did this in my own worktree, `sleepy-gauss-bfc45f`, on a new branch `claude/printer-panel-exit-crash` started at 0e55c4f9be. The changes are in three files: `PrinterPanel.cpp`, `PrinterPanel.hpp` and `tests/shell/shell_harness.cpp`. Expect small merge conflicts when this meets that session's work.

**1. Exit crash: the cause was different from the suspect.** `AgentHost::send_envelope` is not involved. On macOS its scripts run through Orca's `WKWebView_evaluateJavaScript`, which has no completion callback. The debugger showed the actual sequence:
- Orca's `WebView::CreateWebView` connects each new web view to the app a moment after creating it, not immediately.
- On macOS, wxWidgets then runs a script and waits for WebKit's answer in a nested event loop. While it waits, `GUI_App::is_adding_script_handler()` is true.
- The harness opens and then closes the printer panel within one event-loop turn. `PrinterPanel::close()`'s deferred teardown then runs inside that wait and deletes the web view that is still waiting.
- When WebKit shuts down, it answers the wait anyway and calls into the deleted view, which segfaults.

**The fix.** In `PrinterPanel::tear_down_runtime`, if a web view is still being connected, the panel hides the old view and disconnects it from the conversation. It deletes the view and its document on a 50 ms retry timer once the connection has finished. Orca's `GUI_App::run_wizard` already uses the same check for the same reason. The debugger confirmed that the close now takes this deferred path, from exactly the stack that used to crash.

In the real app this is more likely to happen when someone clicks quickly than in normal use. For example, a click that reopens the panel for another printer could land during that brief wait. Other short-lived owners of `AgentWebView` would need the same guard; the printer panel is the only one today.

**2. Stale check.** I didn't need to ask which behavior is intended. The commit message and the code in `PrinterMenu.cpp` both say "Printer settings…" now opens the printer conversation on Home. The harness check now:
- saves the fixture's printer under a name, because only a named printer opens in "change" mode;
- chooses "Printer settings…" from the header's printer menu;
- checks that Home shows the printer panel about that printer and that OrcaSlicer's settings window stays closed;
- closes the panel, returns to the Prepare screen, removes the named printer and restores the original printer;
- continues with the filament check, which still expects OrcaSlicer's settings window.

**A trap in my first baseline.** Building only the `shell_integration_harness` target doesn't build the Home and Agent web pages. Without them no web views exist, so the crash disappears and a different check fails. A fresh build also needs the `jusprin_web` and `jusprin_catalogs` targets.
